about: The common App Store rejections that public repos catalogue, mapped onto the NEXT iOS app (cmux-next-ios; the submission is cmux INTERNAL, dev.cmux.app.internal). Each entry says what the app does today and which deterministic detector of the review gate (.github/workflows/ios-review-gate.yml) catches it: lint:<rule> is a finding of cmux-next-ios/scripts/app_review_gate.py, store-rule:<rule> one of scripts/cmux-next/check-app-store-rules.py, uitest:<func> a UI test, workflow:<name> a step of an ios-*.yml workflow. app_review_gate.py lint fails when an entry names a detector that does not exist, has an unknown status, or is a follow-up that does not say what is left. Our own rejections live in rejection-history.json; this file is everyone else's. new_detector marks the checks added with this file (Leo, 2026-11-22: "THERE ARE ENTIRE REPOS THAT WE CAN MAP FUCKING COMMON REJECTIONS AND APPLY SHIT TO OUR IOS APP").

statuses.gated: a deterministic detector catches it before submission
statuses.not-applicable: the app does not do the thing the rejection is about; the reason says why
statuses.follow-up: a real gap a script cannot close today; follow_up says what is left
statuses.not-deterministic: only a person or a model can judge it; the reason says how it is covered

rejections.title: Reviewer cannot sign in: no demo account or sign-in steps in the review notes
rejections.app_status: review-notes-asc-internal.txt gives a demo account ({{DEMO_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}}, filled at upload) and a path that needs no Mac.

rejections.title: App completeness: crashes, dead buttons, broken flows
rejections.app_status: The gate's device suite taps every control on onboarding, Home and Settings and sends a Chief message.

rejections.title: Placeholder text, lorem ipsum or 'coming soon' in the app or listing
rejections.app_status: None today.

rejections.title: Developer-facing error text shown to the reviewer
rejections.app_status: Three String(describing:) error sites remain (warnings, not blockers).

rejections.title: Export compliance (encryption) not declared
rejections.app_status: ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption is false in project.yml.

rejections.title: Listing mentions other platforms (Android, Google Play)
rejections.app_status: No mention.

rejections.title: Name, subtitle or keywords over the length limits, or stuffed
rejections.app_status: Within limits.

rejections.title: Keywords name competitors or other companies' trademarks
rejections.app_status: Keywords are generic (coding agent, AI agent, developer, ...); none names a company.

rejections.title: Screenshots missing, wrong device size, or not showing the app in use
rejections.app_status: No iPhone screenshots in the repo yet (known blocker, #40927).

rejections.title: Listing describes features (purchases) the submitted build does not have
rejections.app_status: The shared en-US description says the plans are bought in the app, but cmux INTERNAL (appsWithoutSubscriptions) sells nothing. The gate now warns; per-lane metadata is the fix.
rejections.follow_up: Give the internal-submission lane its own description (no purchase claim) or drop the sentence; then make metadata.iap-claim a blocker.

rejections.title: Support URL missing, dead, or without a way to contact the developer
rejections.app_status: https://cmux.com support page; rejected once (rejection-history.json).

rejections.title: Privacy policy missing from the listing
rejections.app_status: privacyPolicyUrl is https://cmux.com/privacy-policy in every locale.

rejections.title: Privacy policy not reachable inside the app
rejections.app_status: Settings and Welcome link the privacy policy.

rejections.title: Account creation without in-app account deletion
rejections.app_status: Settings has Delete Account.

rejections.title: Third-party sign-in without Sign in with Apple (or an equivalent)
rejections.app_status: Sign in with Apple ships beside Google and GitHub.

rejections.title: Missing or vague permission purpose strings (ITMS-90683)
rejections.app_status: Every API the app uses has a specific purpose string.

rejections.title: App breaks or nags when a permission is denied
rejections.app_status: A denied camera explains itself and offers Settings.

rejections.title: A custom pre-permission screen whose button says 'Allow' or blocks progress
rejections.app_status: The app has legitimate Allow buttons (agent permission requests), so a text match would cry wolf; permission prompts come from system APIs at the point of use.
rejections.reason: Judged by the gate's model review of screens, not by a text rule.

rejections.title: Privacy manifest missing or not declaring a required-reason API (ITMS-91053)
rejections.app_status: The app and both notification extensions ship manifests; the app's covers every package it links.

rejections.title: Privacy manifest lists a reason code Apple does not accept for the category, or an SDK-only code (ITMS-91056)
rejections.app_status: All codes are valid.

rejections.title: App Group UserDefaults declared with CA92.1 only (needs 1C8F.1)
rejections.app_status: Was wrong: the app writes and the notification content extension reads push preferences in the App Group defaults with only CA92.1 declared. Fixed in this PR (1C8F.1 added to both manifests).

rejections.title: Collected data types or purposes that are not Apple's identifiers; tracking without domains or ATT
rejections.app_status: Six types, all App Functionality, no tracking.

rejections.title: Third-party SDK on Apple's list shipped without its own privacy manifest (ITMS-91061)
rejections.app_status: The app links no SDK on Apple's list (no Firebase, Sentry, Alamofire, ...); WebRTC and Stack Auth are vendored and covered by the app's manifest.
rejections.reason: asc validate in the gate's submission job reports ITMS-91061 if one is ever added.

rejections.title: Personal data sent to a third-party AI without disclosure and consent
rejections.app_status: Chats, voice calls and attachments go to the user's coding agents and model providers (Claude, Codex, OpenAI realtime). The privacy policy covers it; the app shows no consent screen naming the provider before the first send.
rejections.follow_up: Add a one-time consent sheet that names the AI providers and what is sent, before the first Chief message or voice call; then add a UI test that it appears and that declining sends nothing.

rejections.title: App Privacy (nutrition label) does not match what the app collects
rejections.app_status: The manifest declares email, name, user ID, device ID, photos or videos and other user content. Connectivity incident reports send device model and OS diagnostics, and voice calls send audio.
rejections.follow_up: Check that the App Store Connect label and the manifest declare diagnostics (CmuxConnectivityTelemetry) and audio data; a label lives in App Store Connect, so the gate cannot read it today.

rejections.title: Entitlements or capabilities the app does not use (HealthKit, iCloud, Apple Pay, ...)
rejections.app_status: Every shipping entitlement is used (push, time-sensitive, Sign in with Apple, App Group, associated domains, keychain).

rejections.title: Background modes declared but not used for their purpose
rejections.app_status: Only audio, used by voice calls (AVAudioSession .playAndRecord).

rejections.title: Deprecated UIWebView in the binary (ITMS-90809)
rejections.app_status: WKWebView only.

rejections.title: Private frameworks or symbols
rejections.app_status: None.

rejections.title: App Transport Security disabled or weakened without a reason
rejections.app_status: Only NSAllowsLocalNetworking (the user's own Mac on the LAN), which needs no justification.

rejections.title: Downloading or executing code that changes the app
rejections.app_status: Commands run on the user's Mac; rejected once (rejection-history.json).

rejections.title: VPN APIs without an organization account and a VPN app
rejections.app_status: The VPN extension is kept out of the App Store build; rejected once (rejection-history.json).

rejections.title: Digital goods sold outside In-App Purchase (Stripe links, 'buy on the web')
rejections.app_status: No checkout links; cmux INTERNAL shows the plan read-only.

rejections.title: Subscriptions without restore, price and term disclosure, manage link, terms and privacy links
rejections.app_status: Applies to the App Store build; cmux INTERNAL sells nothing and says so in the review notes.

rejections.title: Upload rejected at processing: unknown background mode, iPad orientations, catalog
rejections.app_status: Passes check-app-store-rules.py.

rejections.title: App fails on Apple's IPv6-only review network
rejections.app_status: Networking uses hostnames through URLSession and Network.framework; LAN pairing may dial IPv4 literals the user's Mac reports.
rejections.reason: Needs a NAT64 run; a source grep for IPv4 literals would flag the legitimate LAN addresses.

rejections.title: Minimum functionality: a thin wrapper or an app useless without other hardware
rejections.app_status: Cloud Chief works without a Mac; rejected once for needing a Mac (rejection-history.json).

rejections.title: Hidden, dormant or undocumented features (feature flags, debug menus)
rejections.app_status: Debug-only entitlements and settings are excluded from the TestFlight configuration.

rejections.title: Listing or app promises features that are not there yet
rejections.app_status: Caught as 'coming soon' text in the listing and the app's strings.

rejections.title: User-generated content without reporting, blocking and moderation
rejections.app_status: No public content: users see only their own and their team's agent sessions.
rejections.reason: No feed, profile or chat between strangers.

rejections.title: Generative AI app offered in China without the local licence
rejections.app_status: Availability is set in App Store Connect, not in the repo.
rejections.reason: Storefront availability is chosen at submission; the release checklist must leave China unticked.
